chunks: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdillah b. Ja'far b. Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them):

Al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) entered one day upon al-Hasan (peace be upon him). When he looked at him, he wept. Al-Hasan said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'I weep for what will be done to you.' Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What will be brought upon me is poison that will be secretly administered, and I will be killed by it. But no day will be like your day, O Abu Abdillah. Thirty thousand men will rush toward you, claiming they are from the community of our grandfather Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and professing the religion of Islam. They will gather to kill you, shed your blood, violate your sanctity, capture your children and women, and plunder your belongings. At that point, the curse will descend upon the Banu Umayya, the sky will rain ashes and blood, and everything will weep for you — even the wild beasts in the deserts and the fish in the seas.'

key_terms.أرض كرب: implied reference to Karbala through the imagery of grief
key_terms.بني أمية: the Banu Umayya — the Umayyad dynasty responsible for the martyrdoms
key_terms.سم يدس: poison secretly administered — a reference to the poisoning of Imam al-Hasan

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say to Imam al-Husayn about the events of Karbala?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, narrated through a chain reaching back to Imam al-Sadiq from his father from his grandfather, Imam al-Husayn (A) visited Imam al-Hasan (A) one day. When he looked at him, he wept. Al-Hasan asked why he was crying, and al-Husayn said he wept for what would be done to him (al-Hasan). Al-Hasan replied that what awaited him was poison that would be secretly administered to kill him, but he told al-Husayn that no day would be like his — thirty thousand men would come against him, claiming to be from the community of their grandfather Muhammad (S) and professing the religion of Islam. They would gather to kill him, shed his blood, violate his sanctity, capture his children and women, and plunder his belongings. At that point, the curse of God would descend upon the Banu Umayya, the sky would rain ashes and blood, and everything would weep for him — even the wild beasts in the deserts and the fish in the seas.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Harun (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far b. Jami` al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (as).

One day, al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) visited al-Hasan (as). When he saw him, he wept. So, he said to him: What makes you weep, O Aba `Abdillah? He said: I weep over what will happen to you. So, al-Hasan (as) said to him: When poison comes to me, I will be killed by it. However, there is no day like your day, O Aba `Abdillah. Thirty thousand men who claim that they are from the Nation of our grandfather, Muhammad (s), and who disguise [themselves with] the religion of Islam will gather to kill you, shed your blood, desecrate your sanctity, take your offspring and your women captive, and pillage your belongings. At that, damnation will fall on the Umayyads and the sky will rain ashes and blood. Everything will weep for you, even the beasts in the wastelands and the whales in the oceans.
